problems.title: Problem 1: Theoretical vs. Experimental Probability
problems.prompt: A fair standard six-sided die is rolled $60$ times. The number $5$ lands face up $14$ times. Compare the theoretical probability $P(5)$ to the experimental probability, and calculate the difference.
problems.problem: A fair standard six-sided die is rolled $60$ times. The number $5$ lands face up $14$ times. Compare the theoretical probability $P(5)$ to the experimental probability, and calculate the difference.
problems.solution: Theoretical $P(5) = \frac{1}{6} \approx 16.7\%$. Experimental $P = \frac{14}{60} = \frac{7}{30} \approx 23.3\%$. The experimental probability exceeded theoretical expectations by $\frac{4}{60} = \frac{1}{15} \approx 6.7\%$.

problems.title: Problem 2: Compound Probability with Tree Diagram
problems.prompt: A bag contains $3$ red marbles and $2$ blue marbles. Two marbles are drawn at random with replacement. What is the probability of drawing at least one blue marble?
problems.problem: A bag contains $3$ red marbles and $2$ blue marbles. Two marbles are drawn at random with replacement. What is the probability of drawing at least one blue marble?
problems.hint: Use the complement rule: $P(\ge 1\text{ blue}) = 1 - P(\text{both red})$.

problems.title: Problem 3: Random Sampling Population Estimate
problems.prompt: In a random sample of $150$ students from a middle school with $900$ students, $42$ students participate in band. Estimate the total number of students in the entire school who participate in band.
